cards.title: Explicit nearly Ramanujan 3-uniform hypergraphs
cards.formal: Construct an explicit infinite family of d-regular 3-uniform hypergraphs satisfying λ≤(2/√d)(1+d^c) for some absolute constant c<0, with sufficiently dense available sizes for the coding applications in the source. Here λ is defined by the trilinear spectral inequality below. The source leaves the family-density and full uniform construction requirements unspecified.
cards.why: Would provide a sparse deterministic sampling object strong enough to improve the parameters of decodable binary codes and small-bias spaces near the Gilbert–Varshamov regime.
cards.status_note: Recovered the exact spectral definition and negative exponent from the conference and March 2022 full versions. The CCC 2026 related-work discussion explicitly preserves the missing-construction issue. The quantitative family-density requirement remains unspecified.

progress.text: The source obtains randomized mixing hypergraphs and proposes the explicit near-Ramanujan spectral family as Open Problem 22.

category_assignment.reason: The main requested object is an explicit spectral hypergraph family for pseudorandom and coding constructions.

importance.reason: A pseudorandom hypergraph construction with concrete consequences for near-optimal small-bias distributions and decodable codes. Existing numerical score retained.

sentences: The desired hypergraphs use ordered triples with uniform marginals in every coordinate.
Their three-way deviation from independent sampling must satisfy a specific ℓ₂–ℓ∞–ℓ₂ inequality.
The target parameter is at most (2/√d)(1+d^c) for a fixed negative c.
Such deterministic families would strengthen constructions of decodable codes and small-bias sets; a 2026 paper still records their absence.
The required density of available sizes and uniform construction interface need specification.

cards.definitions: The source uses ordered triples: a hypergraph has vertex set V={1,…,n} and a collection E of triples (i,j,k)∈V³. It is d-regular if each vertex occurs exactly d times in each of the three coordinate positions, so |E|=nd. Repeated coordinates are allowed; multiplicities, when present as in the source’s symmetrization, are counted in degrees and sums. For x,y,z∈ℝⁿ define T_H(x,y,z)=d^{−1}Σ_{(i,j,k)∈E}xᵢyⱼzₖ−n^{−2}(Σᵢxᵢ)(Σⱼyⱼ)(Σₖzₖ). The hypergraph is λ-spectral if |T_H(x,y,z)|≤λ‖x‖₂‖y‖∞‖z‖₂ for every x,y,z. Euclidean norms on the first and third vectors and the maximum absolute coordinate on the middle vector are essential. The normalized target is 2d^{−1/2}(1+d^c); as d increases, d^c tends to zero. The exponent c is a fixed constant, independent of n and d, and no particular negative value is prescribed. Explicitness calls for a deterministic construction rather than selecting a favorable random hypergraph; the source contrasts it with stronger local-access explicitness but does not fully specify the family’s uniformity and size coverage.
cards.answer_criterion: A complete formulation must specify the available (n,d) pairs, quantitative density of sizes, uniform construction input and output, and deterministic running-time bound. It then requires a constructor whose outputs satisfy coordinatewise regularity and the displayed spectral bound with one fixed c<0, or a refutation under those same conventions. A randomized existence result, ordinary graph expansion or an ℓ₂–ℓ₂–ℓ₂ hypergraph estimate does not meet this target.

context_blocks.title: The hyperedges encode a three-way sampling rule
context_blocks.text: A triple selects three vertices, with every coordinate having a uniform marginal because of regularity. The centered trilinear form measures its deviation from three independent uniform choices.

context_blocks.title: The middle norm is deliberate
context_blocks.text: The source uses ‖y‖∞, not a Euclidean norm divided by √n. Replacing that norm changes the expansion requirement and can make the desired sparsity regime impossible.

context_blocks.title: Random constructions do not supply the requested family
context_blocks.text: The source gives a probabilistic construction with mixing parameter O(1/√d), and converts mixing to spectral control with a logarithmic loss. The requested near-2 leading constant and deterministic construction are additional demands.

context_blocks.title: The coding consequence motivates this exact target
context_blocks.text: Suitable hypergraphs would yield efficiently decodable balanced binary codes with rate near ε² up to logarithmic factors, and corresponding small-bias distributions.

context_blocks.title: The 2026 small-bias improvement does not provide these hypergraphs
context_blocks.text: The later paper improves explicit small-bias sets through a different construction. Its related-work discussion still identifies the needed explicit hypergraphs as unavailable.

context_blocks.title: Remaining specification
context_blocks.text: The source does not quantify “sufficiently dense” for the infinite family: the permitted vertex counts, their gaps, and their dependence on degree must be specified. It also does not give a complete uniform input/output and running-time requirement for the hypergraph constructor across degrees. Requiring all n,d, constant-factor gaps, or a polylogarithmic neighbor oracle would each add a condition not stated in Open Problem 22.

cards.title: An extreme high-end black-box hardness-to-randomness proof
cards.formal: Do there exist black-box construction/reconstruction pairs (Con_ℓ,Red_ℓ) with seed length r=(1+o(1))ℓ, output length m=2^{(1−o(1))ℓ}, advice length a=m^{1+o(1)}=2^{(1−o(1))ℓ}, and worst-case oracle-query count q=m^{o(1)}=2^{o(ℓ)}, such that any distinguisher with advantage greater than 1/10 against Con_ℓ(f) permits exact reconstruction of every Boolean f on ℓ input bits? This recovers the complete parameter list of the source, but the nontrivial slack required for the advice budget still needs specification.
cards.why: Tests the possibility of hardness-to-randomness reductions near their limiting seed and output scales, with a query cost small enough to preserve strong circuit hardness.
cards.status_note: Checked the conference definition, November 2023 full-version restatement and revision history, plus the 2025 targeted-generator model. No general resolution was located through 12 September 2026. The standalone exponent notation needs a precise nontrivial advice-slack convention before being certified as a benchmark.

importance.reason: A basic barrier question for obtaining nearly optimal pseudorandomness from hardness with minimal query loss. Existing numerical score retained.

sentences: The source asks for a construction that turns any candidate hard Boolean function into a candidate generator.
Every distinguisher breaking that generator must permit exact reconstruction of the original function using a single advice string.
The desired seed, output, advice and query parameters are all specified simultaneously at extreme high-end scales.
The construction map itself is allowed to be computationally unrestricted, and later targeted-generator results do not settle this model.
The required fine-scale gap between the advice budget and the full truth-table length needs an explicit convention.

cards.definitions: For integers u,v≥1, let F_{u,v} be all functions {0,1}ᵘ→{0,1}ᵛ. For each input length ℓ, the construction is an arbitrary map Con_ℓ:F_{ℓ,1}→F_{r,m}; write G_f=Con_ℓ(f). No computation-time, circuit-size or oracle-query bound is imposed on this map, and it may depend on the entire truth table of f. A distinguisher is any Boolean function D:{0,1}ᵐ→{0,1}; it breaks G_f if |Pr[D(G_f(U_r))=1]−Pr[D(U_m)=1]|>1/10, where U_t is uniform on {0,1}ᵗ. Red_ℓ is a deterministic oracle procedure receiving x∈{0,1}^ℓ and α∈{0,1}^a, with oracle access only to D. Its correctness condition is ∀f ∀D breaking G_f ∃α ∀x: Red_ℓ^D(x,α)=f(x). The same α serves every x and may depend on f,D; it is not fresh per input. The procedure may make adaptive queries and must halt using at most q queries for every D,α,x, including choices for which correctness is not required. Only queries are charged; unrestricted finite computation and nonuniform dependence on ℓ are allowed in this combinatorial model. The four parameter sequences depend only on ℓ, and all little-o terms tend to zero as ℓ→∞. In particular r/ℓ→1, (log₂m)/ℓ→1, (log₂a)/(log₂m)→1 and (log₂q)/ℓ→0 (with q≥1 permitted as a bound). Exact reconstruction corresponds to worst-case hardness, not merely agreement on most x. The displayed exponent limits alone do not specify how far a must remain below 2^ℓ.
cards.answer_criterion: After fixing the missing quantitative advice-slack convention, give pairs satisfying the same simultaneous parameter bounds and the full ∀f ∀D ∃α ∀x correctness condition, or rule out all such pairs. Failure of one construction family, an average-case reconstruction theorem or a generator targeted to one input is not a complete negative or positive answer to this universal black-box question.

context_blocks.title: This is a reduction question rather than a hardness assumption
context_blocks.text: The pair must work for every candidate Boolean function f. Its role is that any successful generator distinguisher can be converted into a procedure computing f exactly, using advice and black-box access to that distinguisher.

context_blocks.title: Every parameter is near a limiting scale
context_blocks.text: The seed is only slightly longer than ℓ, the output and advice lengths have exponent approaching ℓ, and the reconstruction procedure uses a subpolynomial number of queries in the output length. Dropping any of those requirements changes the source question.

context_blocks.title: Construction efficiency is deliberately absent
context_blocks.text: The source explicitly allows arbitrary Con maps to make its black-box lower-bound model broad. A positive answer here would be necessary for the proposed derandomization application, but would not by itself give an efficiently computable generator.

context_blocks.title: Known barriers concern restricted kinds of proofs
context_blocks.text: The source proves limitations for certain construction properties and hardness-amplification settings. Its November 2023 full version still explicitly leaves the general parameterized black-box question open.

context_blocks.title: Later fast derandomization has a different guarantee
context_blocks.text: The 2025 paper obtains targeted generators under hardness conditions over samplable distributions. That progress does not claim this single construction map and exact reconstruction guarantee for all candidate f and all breaking D.

context_blocks.title: Remaining quantitative convention
context_blocks.text: The exponent-level notation a=m^{1+o(1)}=2^{(1−o(1))ℓ} does not quantify the required slack between advice length a and the full truth-table length 2^ℓ. Proposition 1.8 motivates the question through useful hardness transfer with a+qm below the available circuit hardness, but Open Problem 9 does not prescribe that slack as part of its standalone parameter list. A precise nondegenerate benchmark must state this additional quantitative convention; it must not silently fix a≤2^ℓ/10 or another arbitrary margin.

meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. We aim for benchmarks of 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. All three use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The possible 1,000-problem expansion has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The targets are 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. Top 100, Top 500 and the possible Top 1000 use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
